Both the winners and the runners-up qualified for the four-team [[2026 Supercopa de España]]. [[Athletic Bilbao]] were the defending champions, having beaten [[RCD Mallorca|Mallorca]] in the [[2024 Copa del Rey final|final of the previous edition]], but were eliminated in the round of 16 by [[CA Osasuna|Osasuna]].{{cite web|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2024/apr/07/athletic-club-beat-mallorca-in-copa-del-rey-final-to-end-40-year-trophy-drought|title=Athletic Club beat Mallorca in Copa del Rey final to end 40-year trophy drought|date=7 April 2023|first=Sid |last=Lowe|work=The Guardian|access-date=8 April 2024}}{{cite web|url= https://www.espn.com/soccer/report/_/gameId/699336|title=Athletic Club beat Mallorca for 1st Copa del Rey in 40 years|date=7 April 2023|work=ESPN|access-date=8 April 2024}} The [[2025 Copa del Rey final|final]] was held at [[Estadio de La Cartuja|La Cartuja]] in [[Seville]] between [[FC Barcelona|Barcelona]] and [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]] on 26 April 2025, with the Catalans defeating their [[El Clásico|rivals]] 3–2 after extra time for a record-extending 32nd title. As winners, Barcelona were assured a place in the [[2025–26 UEFA Europa League#League phase|2025–26 UEFA Europa League league phase]]; however, since they had already qualified for European competition via [[2024–25 La Liga|league standings]], their place was passed down to the seventh-placed team in La Liga and the UEFA Conference League spot reserved for the seventh-placed team was awarded to the team who finished eighth in the league. As across Spain, match times up to 26 October 2024 and from 30 March 2025 are [[Central European Summer Time|CEST]] ([[UTC+02:00|UTC+2]]). Times on interim ("winter") days are [[Central European Time|CET]] ([[UTC+01:00|UTC+1]]).
